bounds: characters of one keymap line
set_by: 0x00198210 reads each line with getline(stream, buffer, 0x80) (0x00198222)
past_it: a line of 128 or more characters before its line feed or the end of the file: getline stores the first 127, leaves the rest unread and sets the stream's fail bit, and the 127-character part is parsed as a line. A part that is neither a binding nor a header, or a header without ], ends the read as any such line does. A binding value or header number that has no digits stops the game (0x0019858A, 0x0019853F), and so does one too large for an int (0x0019857C, 0x00198531): each is a conversion error. Only a part that parses returns to the loop, and then the loop goes on: every later getline on the failed stream extracts nothing, so the line is empty and skipped (0x0019823D), and it cannot set the end-of-file bit, the only bit the loop tests (0x0019851E) before it reads again (0x00198210), so the read never ends. A line of exactly 127 characters, followed by a line feed or the end of the file, reads normally
